name: staff-scheduler
//overrides: gaxios: reached only through @opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node ->
resource-detector-gcp -> gcp-metadata. Versions below 7.3.0 depend on
rimraf 5, which drags in glob -> minimatch -> brace-expansion <=5.0.7 and
its high-severity DoS advisory (GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg) into the PRODUCTION
tree, failing the CI gate on every PR. 7.3.0 dropped the rimraf dependency
outright, so this pins forward within the same major rather than patching
the leaf. Overriding brace-expansion itself was rejected: the only fixed
release is 5.0.8, and forcing it beneath minimatch 9 (written against 2.x)
crosses a major boundary to reach code that would no longer be installed
at all. Plain `npm audit fix` does not resolve this — gaxios 7.1.3 is a
hard pin from gcp-metadata. Remove once the OpenTelemetry packages
themselves depend on gaxios >= 7.3.0.
exceljs -> archiver -> archiver-utils -> glob pulls minimatch@3.1.5 ->
brace-expansion@1.1.16 into the PRODUCTION tree, matching the same
high-severity DoS advisories above. Keyed on 'minimatch@3.1.5' (an exact
version selector, not a path) rather than on brace-expansion directly:
every minimatch@3.1.5 anywhere in the tree wants brace-expansion ^1.1.7,
so 1.1.18 satisfies it with no major-version jump, while minimatch's 5.x
and later lines — which depend on the incompatible 2.x line of
brace-expansion and appear elsewhere in this same tree — are untouched
because their version does not match the selector. A path-shaped override
was tried first and rejected: hoisting placed the real brace-expansion
node somewhere the declared nesting didn't reach, so npm installed it
unmodified and flagged it invalid instead of applying the override.
